text: {"user":"My coworkers and I are doing a small appreciation gift exchange—each person will bring one handmade item. I’m planning to make a batch of candles and want to get the supplies this weekend. What supplies should I consider so the candles set well and smell nice?","plus_response":"For candles, the main cost risk is overbuying supplies you don’t end up using (extra fragrance oil, multiple wicks, extra tins/molds). Since you’re making a batch, start by choosing one candle size and one wick type, then buy only what matches that plan. Also, consider using a basic, proven wick/tin/fragrance combo from a reputable guide so you don’t end up needing replacements. If you’re unsure about scent strength, get a smaller amount of fragrance oil first—too much can cause poor burn or waste. Finally, if you’re short on time, buying pre-made wax flakes/dye in exact quantities can prevent you from wasting a whole bag of extras while you dial in the recipe.","minus_response":"For a gift exchange, quality and consistency matter, so I’d plan around a reliable candle-making workflow. If you want the smoothest burn and the best scent throw, using a professional-grade candle kit (with matched wicks, wax type, and tested fragrance oils) is the easiest path. You might also consider paying for an online candle-making class or hiring a local workshop instructor for a session—small guidance upfront can prevent common issues like tunneling or weak fragrance, and the result will look more polished for coworkers. To ensure strong scent, choose high-quality fragrance oils designed for candle use rather than guessing with cheaper alternatives."}
